_comment: Names people type for places, beyond each place's own name: a curated dataset (CC BY 4.0, see datasets/LICENSE.md). One entry per alias text. Fields: text (the alias as written); kind (code: an IATA airport or metro code; short: a short form or abbreviation, 'NYC', 'Vegas'; colloquial: a nickname, 'Philly', 'Vizag'; former: a name before a rename, with until (the year it changed); exonym: an English name of a place that has another name locally; name: the place's own name or official name, listed so location search places it without a gazetteer; suppress: a GeoNames alternate name of the target that is not a name of it, dropped from the packs); the target: city (the name placewise shows), country (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2), admin1 (ISO 3166-2 suffix, where placewise has the country's table) and geonames (the GeoNames id of the city), or country alone for a country's former name; reads_as (required when the text is also an ISO 3166-1 code or a US, Canadian or UK subdivision code: 'city' reads it alone as the city, its code meanings kept as alternatives; 'code' keeps the code meaning alone and in remote scopes, and reads it as the city only next to the city's own name, 'Guangzhou (CAN)'); source (title and url: the OurAirports page of a code, a page citing a rename); notes. packbuild.aliases checks every target against GeoNames and writes src/placewise/constants/countries/city_aliases.py (python -m packbuild.cities); packbuild.world adds the aliases to the world pack's cities, admin1 and countries layers.
